inherited.suggestion: 中文改为：“他先列出过警网根本抓不到人的可能，但据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为只能相信装模作样的解释”。英文改为：“…but, finding no torture or false testimony in Jiangxi, concluded that only the explanation of a show was credible.”

contamination.brief_line: 有记录的骨架：作者指出，叫魂案让皇帝有理由对抓不到妖首的地方官发怒，而这样的妖首并不存在(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E1)。弘历在朱批中痛斥河南巡抚“无用废物”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E2)，斥浙江巡抚按例把案子交给臬司(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E3)，痛骂未及时报案的江苏按察使吴坛“不知恩之物”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E4)。作者认为官僚中存在多种抵制，包括可能有官员拒绝迫害无辜(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E5)，且抵制不必串通(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E6)。危机前一年，有人说吴绍诗被称为“老菩萨”，弘历担心他消极误事(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E7)；吴时年七十，出身法律世家，弘历很尊重这个家族(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E8)；高晋说没听说吴不称职，弘历让他留任(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E9)。谣言6月中旬从浙江传入江西，吴未奏报，自称口头命令属下警觉，无人被捕(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E10)；弘历只温和地说“汝误矣”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E11)。10月初吴报告布下比别省更严密的警网，派人改装密查(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E12)，并在奏报中警告“左道邪术”之害，弘历朱批“恐属空言，实难信矣”(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E13)。六个星期后，吴报告江西没有一起剪辫案，档案中没有江西搜捕嫌犯的记录(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E14)。吴安然度过危机，第二年被任命为刑部尚书(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E16)。对照：其子吴坛同样未报案而遭痛斥(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E17)，三周后查出苏州城外十一座经堂(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E18)；收场时，未及时奏报的苏尔德被贬往新疆(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E19)。

必须写明的不确定性：本文唯一依据是孔飞力《叫魂》中译本（陈兼、刘昶译），这是一部学术史著作，没有使用其他史源。朱批和奏报文字据本书引用（中译本文字，E13中“矣口”照书中原样），是否与档案原文逐字一致无法从本书判断。“吴绍诗根本不打算查缉、部署只是装模作样”是作者的推断(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E15)，作者自己也提出另一种可能，即警网根本抓不到人(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E15)，文章只能写“作者认为……”。吴升官的原因，作者也只是推测可能与他的法律造诣和高晋的袒护有关(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E16)。高晋答应的后续报告作者未能找到(BK-JIAOHUN-U141-E9)。不要替吴绍诗或弘历写心理活动。年份照书中写法使用，不要另做换算。

issues.problem: “从浙江传进了江西”/“crossed from Zhejiang into Jiangxi”沿用了已知污染K1的说法。证据只写谣言经信江河谷这条通往浙江的通道传入江西，没有写谣言来自浙江。下一句已经交代了这条通道，所以这半句也是重复。

evidence.quote: 江西东面的信江河谷是连接邻省浙江的便捷通道，叫魂的谣言早在6月中旬就从这里悄悄地传人了江西

issues.proposed: 中文改为“1768年6月中旬，叫魂的谣言传进了江西。”英文改为“In the middle of June 1768, rumours of soulstealing reached Jiangxi.”后句保留。
issues.rationale: 删去“从浙江”/“from Zhejiang”。证据只说谣言经信江河谷这条通往浙江的通道传入江西，没有说谣言来自浙江。英文第二句补出“of Zhejiang”，与中文“邻省浙江”保持一致。

issues.problem: “只回了一句「汝误矣」”/“wrote a single line”断言弘历的回应只有这一句。证据只说弘历“只是温和地驳斥了他”，并引了“汝误矣”，没有说回应只有一句。

evidence.quote: 只是温和地驳斥了他：对谣言来加奏报是“汝误矣”

issues.proposed: 中文改为“弘历只是温和地驳斥他：「汝误矣」，意思是你做错了。”英文改为“the emperor rebuked him only mildly: "You were wrong."”
issues.rationale: 把“只回了一句”改为“只是温和地驳斥他”，英文同步改写。同时删去重复的“这是驳斥，却只是温和的一句”，不再断言回应只有一句。

issues.problem: 英文把吴绍诗奏报里的部署写成了已经发生的事实，并把“每旬报告”指定为密查人员所报。“they reported every ten days”和“The search ran from religious houses ... into the remotest forest”都是这种写法。证据只是吴绍诗报告中的安排，没有写明由谁报告；孔飞力还提出这张警网可能从未动用过。中文“从寺庙道观……一直查到深山密林”也宜明确为奏报所说的查访范围。

evidence.quote: 并每旬一次报告有无可疑人物
要么是吴的警网从来就没有真正地动用过

issues.proposed: 英文改为“with a report every ten days on whether anyone suspicious had appeared”，删去“The search ran from ... forest.”或改为“The places named ran from religious houses ... to the remotest forest.”中文末句改为“查访范围从寺庙道观、祠堂书馆，一直到深山密林”。
issues.rationale: 英文改为“with a report every ten days”，不再指定由谁报告。末句改为奏报所列的查访地点范围，不写成实际执行的搜查。中文末句同样改为“查访范围从……一直到深山密林”。

issues.problem: “报告里还有一段警告”把E13的警告和朱批直接归入10月初那份警网报告，并说朱批“针对的正是这份奏报”/“aimed squarely at this report”。证据没有说明E13出自哪一份奏报；孔飞力只称之为“先前奏报”中的警告。

evidence.quote: 他在先前奏报中提出的忧心忡忡的警告和精心布置的查缉

issues.proposed: 中文改为“吴绍诗的奏报里还有一段警告”，末句改为“这是一句明白的怀疑。”英文改为“In his memorials Wu Shaoshi also issued a warning.”，末句改为“It was open doubt.”
issues.rationale: 开头改为“吴绍诗的奏报里还有一段警告”/“In his memorials Wu Shaoshi also issued a warning”，不再把这段警告归入10月初那份报告。末句删去“针对的正是这份奏报”/“aimed squarely at this report”。

issues.problem: “弘历在那份奏报上写下了「恐属空言」”/“on that very report”同样把朱批固定在某一份奏报上，证据不支持。

evidence.quote: 朱批：“恐属空言，实难信矣口”

issues.proposed: 中文改为“弘历在吴绍诗的警告旁批下了「恐属空言」”。英文改为“Hongli wrote "I fear these are empty words" beside Wu Shaoshi's warning.”
issues.rationale: 把“在那份奏报上”/“on that very report”改为“在吴绍诗的这段警告上”/“in response to Wu Shaoshi's warning”。证据只显示这条朱批批在这段警告上，不能固定到某一份奏报。

issues.problem: “倾向于装模作样的解释”/“leaned toward”弱化了孔飞力的说法。孔飞力据江西没有刑求和伪证，说的是“只能相信”。这也与analysis.0的转述不一致。

evidence.quote: 据此，我们只能相信，巡抚吴绍诗根本就不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子

issues.proposed: 中文改为“但据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为只能相信装模作样的解释”。英文改为“but, finding no torture or false testimony in Jiangxi, concluded that only the explanation of a show was credible.”
issues.rationale: 把“倾向于”/“leaned toward”改为孔飞力的原有说法：他据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为“只能相信”。这样也与analysis.0的转述一致。

issues.problem: 末句“他先列出过……认为只能相信前一种”与本段前文重复，读起来像核查说明。
issues.proposed: 末句只保留“这是孔飞力的推断，不是档案记载。”英文同步删去最后一句。

issues.problem: story.6已经写到10月之后六个星期，story.7又回到9月28日，读者可能误以为吴坛查经堂发生在江西报告之后。
issues.proposed: 开头改为“早在9月底，吴坛走的是另一条路。”英文改为“Back in late September, Wu Tan went another way.”

issues.problem: uncertainty_note与limits.0基本重复：唯一依据、装模作样是推断、高晋袒护是推测。
issues.proposed: 只保留关于“口”字照录的说明，其余删去，因为limits已有。

issues.problem: hook.1重复了dek的前提，即追捕不存在的妖首、抓不到人挨骂，摘要与开头有部分重叠。
issues.proposed: 可以把dek的前半句改为只提处境，例如“皇帝追得很紧，巡抚们怎么回话都可能挨骂”，把“妖首并不存在”留给hook.1。

issues.problem: 英文“feared that a purge would endanger their careers”把“清剿”（对妖党的清剿，全文英文作campaign/suppression）译成purge，容易被读成对官员的整肃，与中文意思不一致。

evidence.quote: 害怕清剿会危及自己的仕途

issues.proposed: 改为“feared that the suppression campaign would endanger their careers”。
issues.rationale: 把英文“a purge”改为“the suppression campaign”。这里的清剿指对妖党的清剿，不是对官员的整肃，改后与中文意思和全文用词一致。

issues.problem: limits 把孔飞力的结论写成“倾向于装模作样的解释”（英文 leaned toward），弱化了原文的说法。原文是据江西没有刑求和伪证而“只能相信”。analysis.0 的转述是对的，limits 与之不一致。
issues.rationale: 问题成立：孔飞力原文是“只能相信”，limits写成“倾向于”弱化了他的说法。已列为F6。

issues.problem: 本段前文已写明这是孔飞力的推断（“孔飞力摆出两种可能……于是推断……”）。末句“这是孔飞力的推断，不是档案记载；他先列出过……认为只能相信前一种”把同一推理链几乎原样重复了一遍，读起来像正文里插进的核查说明（第8条），而且与 limits.0、uncertainty_note 重复。英文末两句同样如此。

evidence.quote: 要么是吴的警网从来就没有真正地动用过，要么就是这样的警网根本就捕捉不到嫌犯

issues.proposed: 删去中文末句“这是孔飞力的推断，不是档案记载；他先列出过警网根本捕捉不到嫌犯的可能，但据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为只能相信前一种。”英文同步删去“That is Kuhn's inference, not something the archives record. He first named … was credible.”这两句。
issues.rationale: 删去中文末句“这是孔飞力的推断，不是档案记载；他先列出过……认为只能相信前一种”，英文同步删去末两句。前文已用“孔飞力摆出两种可能……于是推断”交代了这是孔飞力的推断及其推理链，末句属于重复的核查说明，且与 limits.0、uncertainty_note 重复。其余句子未改动。

edits.before: In the middle of June 1768, rumours of soulstealing crossed from Zhejiang into Jiangxi. They came through the Xin River valley on Jiangxi's eastern side, the easy route into the neighbouring province. The governor of Jiangxi, Wu Shaoshi, was about seventy. The rumours had entered his jurisdiction, and he sent no report to the court.
edits.after: In the middle of June 1768, rumours of soulstealing reached Jiangxi. They came through the Xin River valley on Jiangxi's eastern side, the easy route into the neighbouring province of Zhejiang. The governor of Jiangxi, Wu Shaoshi, was about seventy. The rumours had entered his jurisdiction, and he sent no report to the court.

edits.before: 回到6月。谣言入境，吴绍诗没有奏报。他后来向弘历报告说，自己曾口头命令属下留意可疑的行旅，但没有人被捕，省内也没有发现剪辫的事。对他不奏报谣言，弘历只回了一句「汝误矣」，意思是你做错了。这是驳斥，却只是温和的一句。孔飞力说，弘历对这位年高誉隆的巡抚表现出了出乎意料的克制。
edits.after: 回到6月。谣言入境，吴绍诗没有奏报。他后来向弘历报告说，自己曾口头命令属下留意可疑的行旅，但没有人被捕，省内也没有发现剪辫的事。对他不奏报谣言，弘历只是温和地驳斥他：「汝误矣」，意思是你做错了。孔飞力说，弘历对这位年高誉隆的巡抚表现出了出乎意料的克制。

edits.before: Back to June. The rumours had crossed the border, and Wu Shaoshi sent no report. He later told Hongli that he had verbally ordered his subordinates to keep an eye on suspicious travellers, but no one had been arrested and no cases of queue-clipping had turned up in the province. On the failure to report the rumours, the emperor wrote a single line: "You were wrong." It was a rebuke, but a mild one. Kuhn calls it an unexpected show of restraint toward an elderly and highly respected governor.

On the failure to report the rumours, the emperor rebuked him only mildly: "You were wrong." Kuhn calls it an unexpected show of restraint toward an elderly and highly respected governor.

edits.before: 到了10月初，吴绍诗交上一份很不一样的报告。他说自己在省内布下了一张比任何别省都严密的警网：挑选干员「改装易姓」，换了装束、改了姓名，分赴各县秘密查缉，每旬报告一次有无可疑人物；又令各府州派精细强干的人，去查访「庵观寺院祠堂书馆及深山密箐等处」，从寺庙道观、祠堂书馆，一直查到深山密林。
edits.after: 到了10月初，吴绍诗交上一份很不一样的报告。他说自己在省内布下了一张比任何别省都严密的警网：挑选干员「改装易姓」，换了装束、改了姓名，分赴各县秘密查缉，每旬报告一次有无可疑人物；又令各府州派精细强干的人，去查访「庵观寺院祠堂书馆及深山密箐等处」，查访范围从寺庙道观、祠堂书馆，一直到深山密林。

edits.before: In early October, Wu Shaoshi sent in a very different kind of report. He said he had spread a net across his province tighter than any other province's. He had picked capable agents who would "change their dress and take other surnames," so that they could travel in disguise and search each county in secret, and they reported every ten days on whether anyone suspicious had appeared. He had also ordered each prefecture and department to send sharp, able men to search "convents, temples and monasteries, ancestral halls, schools, and deep mountains and dense thickets." The search ran from religious houses and ancestral halls out into the remotest forest.

The places named ran from religious houses and ancestral halls to the remotest forest.

edits.before: 报告里还有一段警告。他说那些从事「左道邪术」的人，借创立烧香好善会的名义，「阳则聚集乡愚男妇，阴则勾结亡命棍徒」，明面上聚集乡间男女，暗地里勾结亡命之徒；又借避灾防盗之名，造作妖言、制备军器、诱人归附。他要求不论僧道还是其他人，凡是面生可疑、神气沮丧、迁徙无定、怕见人的，都要立即报告地方官。弘历的朱批是：「恐属空言，实难信矣口」，恐怕只是空话，实在难以相信。这是一句明白的怀疑，针对的正是这份奏报。

edits.before: The report also carried a warning. Practitioners of "heterodox ways and evil arts," it said, set up incense-burning charitable societies as a front, "openly gathering ignorant village men and women, secretly colluding with desperadoes and ruffians." On the pretext of warding off disaster and bandits, they spread wicked talk, stockpiled weapons and drew people into their following. Wu Shaoshi ordered that anyone, monk, Daoist priest or layman, who was an unfamiliar face, looked dejected, kept moving from place to place, or avoided being seen, be reported to the local officials at once. Hongli's rescript read: "I fear these are empty words; truly hard to believe." It was open doubt, aimed squarely at this report.

edits.before: 本文唯一的依据是孔飞力《叫魂》的中译本（陈兼、刘昶译），没有使用其他史源。朱批和奏报都转引自书中译文，与档案原文是否逐字一致无法判断。“只是装模作样”是孔飞力的推断，他先列出过警网根本抓不到人的可能，但倾向于装模作样的解释；吴绍诗为何难以受罚，孔飞力归于他的法律造诣，并推测可能还有高晋的袒护。高晋答应的后续报告，孔飞力没有找到。

edits.before: This article rests entirely on the Chinese translation of Kuhn's Soulstealers, by Chen Jian and Liu Chang, and uses no other source. The rescripts and memorials are quoted as they appear in that translation, so I cannot tell whether they match the archival originals word for word, and the English renderings here are translations of that Chinese text. The claim that Wu Shaoshi was merely putting on a show is Kuhn's inference. Kuhn first named the possibility that the net simply could not catch anyone, but leaned toward the explanation that it was a show. As for why Wu Shaoshi was hard to punish, Kuhn attributes it to his legal expertise and conjectures that Gao Jin's protection may also have played a part. Kuhn was unable to find the follow-up report Gao Jin promised.
edits.after: This article rests entirely on the Chinese translation of Kuhn's Soulstealers, by Chen Jian and Liu Chang, and uses no other source. The rescripts and memorials are quoted as they appear in that translation, so I cannot tell whether they match the archival originals word for word, and the English renderings here are translations of that Chinese text. The claim that Wu Shaoshi was merely putting on a show is Kuhn's inference. Kuhn first named the possibility that the net simply could not catch anyone, but, finding no torture or false testimony in Jiangxi, concluded that only the explanation of a show was credible. As for why Wu Shaoshi was hard to punish, Kuhn attributes it to his legal expertise and conjectures that Gao Jin's protection may also have played a part. Kuhn was unable to find the follow-up report Gao Jin promised.

edits.before: Nor is this a story of a wise man outwitting a tyrant. Kuhn lists several forms that bureaucratic resistance may have taken. Some was deliberate. Some came from sluggish procedures that kept officials from reacting to an emergency in time. Some officials, doubting the whole thing, may have refused to take the cases seriously. Others may have feared that a purge would endanger their careers. And some upright officials may have refused to persecute innocent people on the strength of false accusations. Kuhn writes that these actions do not look coordinated, and that resisting despotic power does not require collusion. This article cannot say which of these describes Wu Shaoshi. Kuhn also cautions that saying Hongli "used" political crime is no closer to the truth than saying political crime "used" him. My own reading is that the quiet in Jiangxi and the seventy arrests in Suzhou came out of the same structure. What differed was how each official handled the same pressure.
edits.after: Nor is this a story of a wise man outwitting a tyrant. Kuhn lists several forms that bureaucratic resistance may have taken. Some was deliberate. Others may have feared that the suppression campaign would endanger their careers. And some upright officials may have refused to persecute innocent people on the strength of false accusations. Kuhn writes that these actions do not look coordinated, and that resisting despotic power does not require collusion. This article cannot say which of these describes Wu Shaoshi. Kuhn also cautions that saying Hongli "used" political crime is no closer to the truth than saying political crime "used" him. My own reading is that the quiet in Jiangxi and the seventy arrests in Suzhou came out of the same structure. What differed was how each official handled the same pressure.

edits.before: 江西到底发生了什么？孔飞力摆出两种可能：要么这张警网从来没有真正动用过，要么它根本捕捉不到嫌犯。他注意到，江西看不到其他省份那种刑求和伪证，于是推断吴绍诗根本不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子，那些忧心忡忡的警告和精心的布置都只是「装模作样」。这是孔飞力的推断，不是档案记载；他先列出过警网根本捕捉不到嫌犯的可能，但据江西没有刑求和伪证，认为只能相信前一种。
edits.after: 江西到底发生了什么？孔飞力摆出两种可能：要么这张警网从来没有真正动用过，要么它根本捕捉不到嫌犯。他注意到，江西看不到其他省份那种刑求和伪证，于是推断吴绍诗根本不打算查缉这个他认为是误传的案子，那些忧心忡忡的警告和精心的布置都只是「装模作样」。

edits.before: What actually happened in Jiangxi? Kuhn sets out two possibilities: either the net was never really put to use, or it was incapable of catching anyone. He observes that Jiangxi shows none of the torture and false testimony found in other provinces, and from this he concludes that Wu Shaoshi never intended to pursue a case he believed rested on false rumour. In Kuhn's view, the anxious warnings and the elaborate deployment were only a performance. That is Kuhn's inference, not something the archives record. He first named the possibility that the net could not catch anyone, but on the absence of torture and false testimony concluded that only the first explanation was credible.
